classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a quadratic trajectory, find its intercept and maximum, convert metres to kilometres and solve for two equal-height positions.

content.prompt: A weather rocket is fired so that it follows a parabolic path, just over weather balloons $A$ and $B$, as shown. It has been fired to follow the path with equation $y=\frac15x-\frac1{50}x^2$, where $x$ and $y$ are measured in kilometres.

spec.description: Downward-opening trajectory with positive axis arrows, two equal-height balloon points, right intercept C and a y-axis mark H at maximum height. No numerical ticks or grid. The source origin O label is retained because part a explicitly references the distance from O to C.
spec.mathematics: The curve is y=x/5-x^2/50 on 0≤x≤10. A and B lie on opposite branches at equal heights; H marks the vertex height.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied symbolic labels appear; numerical intercepts, coordinates and maximum height remain hidden.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find how far the rocket travels horizontally from $O$ to point $C$.

answer.worked:
At $C$, $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac15x-\frac1{50}x^2\\0&=x(10-x)\\x&=0\text{ or }x=10.\end{align*}$$
The intercept $x=0$ is the launch point, so the horizontal distance to $C$ is $10\text{ km}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $H$ kilometres, the maximum height reached by the rocket.

answer.worked:
The axis of symmetry lies halfway between the intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+10}{2}\\x&=5.\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens downwards, so its vertex gives the maximum height.
$$\begin{align*}H&=\frac15(5)-\frac1{50}(5)^2\\H&=0.5\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: are both at a height of 200 metres:

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of $A$ and $B$, expressing your answer correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
The balloon height is $200\text{ m}=0.2\text{ km}$.
$$\begin{align*}0.2&=\frac15x-\frac1{50}x^2\\10&=10x-x^2\\x^2-10x&=-10\\x^2-10x+25&=15\\(x-5)^2&=15\\x-5&=\pm\sqrt{15}\\x&=5\pm\sqrt{15}.\end{align*}$$
Point $A$ lies on the ascending branch and $B$ on the descending branch. Thus, to two decimal places, $A=(1.13,0.20)$ and $B=(8.87,0.20)$, with coordinates in kilometres.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence, find the horizontal distance, $AB$, between the balloons, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Use the exact horizontal coordinates before rounding:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=(5+\sqrt{15})-(5-\sqrt{15})\\AB&=2\sqrt{15}\\AB&\approx7.75\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
